propositions: Rebar must safely delegate credential issuance, retrieval, persistence, refresh, and rotation to upstream SDKs, helpers, CI systems, and deployments rather than implementing a universal secret broker or credential store.

Operation snapshots must be structurally unable to contain raw secrets; credentials are provider-native capabilities injected only into typed adapter-specific factories that construct and own the official SDK client.

Static secret materialization and rotation is deployment and restart-based; Rebar reads exactly one of file path or multiline environment value at startup, validates it, stores it in a process-owned 0700 directory, and removes global os.environ mutation and runtime cloud-secret retrieval.

Subprocess environment inheritance preserves native Git, SSH, AWS, proxy, and CA credential chains; Rebar-materialized static secrets are overlaid only onto their owning child adapter and exact sibling-secret variable names are removed from unrelated children without global allowlist.

Unavoidable provider-specific static credentials use Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes only inside non-serializable adapter-local containers with repr/comparison/hash exclusion; the value is unwrapped only at the sending adapter boundary.

Deployment step, container, and service scoping provide the primary secret isolation boundary; Rebar owns only fail-closed provider selection, trusted typed bindings, operation-scoped construction, and leakage prevention verified by canary tests.
